_comment: UC-BANK-02 Bank Counter. No real bank is named anywhere, by rule. The clerk is friendly and a little brisk, the way a real counter is.
hook: The bank. There is a queue, a ceiling fan, and a clerk who has done this ten thousand times. Your documents are in your folder.
summary: You have an account in your own name.

clerk.which: “Which account do you want to open?”
clerk.form: “Fill this in. Take your time, people get the nominee bit wrong.”
clerk.kit: “Passbook, card, and your PIN. Do not write the PIN on the card.”

savings.blurb: Earns interest. You must keep {minimum} in it at all times, or they charge you {charge} a month.

zero_balance.blurb: No minimum. No charge for falling below it, because there is nothing to fall below. Earns the same interest.

minor.blurb: For under-18s. A parent or guardian signs with you. No minimum balance.

warning.cannot_maintain: You earn about {income} a month. Keeping {minimum} sitting in the account at all times would be most of it — and the month you dip below, they take {charge}.

form.title: Account opening form
form.name: Your name
form.nominee_why: The person the bank gives your money to if something happens to you. Without one, your family needs court papers to get it.

pin.title: Set your PIN
pin.prompt: Four digits. Not your birth year.
pin.passerby: Someone has stopped behind you to look at the queue display.
pin.covered: You turned your shoulder and carried on.
pin.weak: That is one of the first PINs anyone would try. Pick another.
pin.done: PIN set. Never tell it to anyone — not a friend, not someone who calls saying they are from the bank.

deposit.prompt: You have {amount} on you. How much goes into the account today?

sms.arrived: A message arrives before you are out of the door: “Dear customer, your KYC is incomplete. Click here to update or your account will be blocked.”
sms.note: You just finished your KYC at the counter. You will meet this message again.

concept.account: A bank account in your own name means your money is yours: it is safe, it is recorded, and a scholarship or salary can be paid into it.
